title: Convergent "Operator Kit" task runtime for safe quick-fix orchestrations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Build a lightweight 'Operator Kit' task runtime that converts curated admin utilities and troubleshooting procedures into composable, auditable tasks. The runtime materializes runbooks-as-tasks (atomic steps, typed inputs, and idempotent adapters) and exposes a safe autop-run surface for first-line responders and automated responders.

Background & problem:
We have many ad-hoc admin helpers (scripts, one-off runbooks) used by SRE/support. They lack a consistent execution model: telemetry, dry-run, RBAC gating, audit trails, and step-level retries. This causes inconsistent MTTR, noisy telemetry, and occasional unsafe fixes in production.

Goals (MVP):
- Define a minimal task schema for operator kits: typed params, expected side-effects, rollback hints, and idempotency markers.
- Implement a runtime service that executes tasks with safety rails: RBAC pre-check, dry-run simulation, explicit confirmation step for high-impact actions, and automatic reversion hooks where available.
- Integrate telemetry: emit structured events (task.start, task.step.complete, task.rollback, task.metrics) to internal observability.
- Ensure auditability and provenance: log inputs, outputs, commit PR id, and user identity tied to SSO.
- Provide a developer flow to author kits (YAML + test harness) and a UI shim in the Console for one-click run/dry-run.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full visual workflow editor.
- Rewriting existing large runbooks — we'll onboard incrementally.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Task schema (docs) and validator exist in repo (contrib/operator-kits/schema.md).
2) Runtime can execute 3 curated operator kits: "rotate-keys-safe", "cache-evict-segmented", "scale-dedicated-pool" with dry-run and confirm flows.
3) All task runs generate telemetry and are visible via an observability dashboard (link below).
4) Security review completed and canary rollout plan approved by security.
5) Mean time to repair (MTTR) for supported incidents is reduced in benchmark runbook tests by 15% vs ad-hoc scripts.

Technical approach:
- Task schema: small YAML shape (id, description, inputs{type,default,validators}, steps[], impact_score, rollback_hint, required_role). We'll use the existing runlet param types as inspiration but keep schema stricter to enable dry-run simulation.
- Runtime: Go microservice that consumes task manifests from git (operator-kits/), validates signatures, compiles steps into an execution graph, and invokes adapters (k8s client, infra API, redis control plane). Execution engine supports step-level retry/backoff, circuit-breaker for high-impact steps, and an opt-in atomic transaction mode for supported systems.
- Safety rails: integrate SSO/SCIM for identity, require 'confirm' for tasks with impact_score > 5, implement RBAC check against existing policy service, and sandboxed dry-run by default for users below 'ops-lead' role.
- Telemetry: structured spans/events sent to tracing + tokenized metrics for cost/latency. Events include task_id, run_id, initiator, step_id, step_outcome, approximated_cost.
- Console integration: small Console panel to list operator kits, run details, dry-run toggles, and last-run provenance.

Operational plan & rollout:
- Phase 1 (2 sprints): schema + runtime prototype + three kits + unit/integration tests + Confluence PR (docs/operator-kits-v1).
- Phase 2 (1 sprint): security review + telemetry dashboard + canary internal rollout to SRE team + synthetic MTTR benchmark.
- Phase 3 (1 sprint): Console UI + broader beta + onboarding docs and authoring template.

Risks & mitigations:
- Unsafe automated fixes: mitigate by defaulting to dry-run and requiring explicit confirmation for high-impact tasks; add policy enforcement.
- Telemetry overhead: sample low-frequency runs and aggregate step metrics to reduce cardinality.
- Dependency sprawl: require adapters to be lightweight and reviewed; provide shimbed test harness to simulate downstream APIs.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/ops/operator-kits-design (draft)
- GitHub prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator-kits (branch: runtime-proto)
- Dashboard prototype (Observability): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/opkits/runs
- Safety checklist PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/412

Next steps:
- Spike: build a PoC runtime that runs a simple 'echo' step and emits telemetry (owner: Diego) — due 2026-03-01.
- Schedule security sync and SRE demo week for 2026-03-08.
- Create authoring template and tests in the repo (owner: Ava).
